Name: icml-repro-20hdQQQrA4-arc
Title: CAffNet: Hard Constraint-Affine Neural Networks
Abstract: Reproduction of anchored claims from 'CAffNet: Hard Constraint-Affine Neural Networks' (ICML 2026).
Experiment:
Reproducibility task: verify the anchored claims of 'CAffNet: Hard Constraint-Affine Neural Networks' (ICML 2026, arXiv 2605.24437) on CPU.

For each claim below, write a self-contained verify_claim<N>.py using only numpy/scipy/sympy (CPU),
run it, save outputs to results/claim<N>.json, and report a verdict (verified/falsified/toy/inconclusive).
Honest boundary: if data/GPU required, report inconclusive — do NOT fabricate toy data.

Claim 1 (Theorem 3.5): Theorem 3.5 proves that if the unconstrained network class universally approximates the target function class F, then CAffNet universally approximates the constrained target class {f_t in F | A(x) f_t <= b(x)}, with approximation error bound ||P* - f_t||_p < (3 + 3*sqrt(n_out))K (Theorem 3.5).
Claim 2 (Section 3): The CAffine layer's projection formula includes a trainable null-space component w_phi(x), P_gamma(x) = f_theta(x) - A_gamma^dagger(x)(A_gamma(x) f_theta(x) - b_gamma(x)) + (I - A_gamma^dagger(x) A_gamma(x)) w_phi(x), allowing joint optimization across multiple feasible projections rather than a fixed orthogonal projection (Section 3).
Claim 3 (Section 3): Unlike prior work (HardNet), CAffNet guarantees hard constraint satisfaction A(x)y <= b(x) without requiring A(x) to have full row rank, and handles arbitrary constraint cardinality via decomposition into sub-constraint combinations of at most min(m, n_out) constraints (Section 3).
Claim 4 (): On the piecewise-constraint benchmark, CAffNet-TF (transformer variant) achieves a 73.33% MSE reduction relative to a soft-constrained neural network baseline while incurring zero constraint violations (Section on Experiments, piecewise constraints task).
Claim 5 (): In the safety-critical control experiment, CAffNet successfully avoids obstacles whereas both HardNet and the soft-constrained baseline fail to do so (Section on Experiments, safety-critical control task).
